name: caveman
description: >
  Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts output tokens 65% (measured) by speaking like caveman
  while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra,
  wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra.
  Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens",
  "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
---

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked â€” quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) â€” tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (â†’) either â€” own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese â†’ reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish â†’ reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim â€” unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only â€” never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |
| **ultra** | Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X â†’ Y) â€” measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully æ–‡è¨€æ–‡. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (ä¹‹/ä¹ƒ/ç‚º/å…¶) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example â€” "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`."

- wenyan-full: "æ¯ç¹ªæ–°ç”Ÿå°è±¡åƒç…§ï¼Œæ•…é‡ç¹ªï¼›ä»¥ useMemo åŒ…ä¹‹å‰‡å…ã€‚"
- wenyan-ultra: "æ–°åƒç…§å‰‡é‡ç¹ªã€‚useMemo åŒ…ä¹‹ã€‚"

Example â€” "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No per-request handshake."
- wenyan-full: "æ± è“„å·²é–‹ä¹‹é€£ï¼Œä¸é€è«‹è€Œæ–°é–‹ï¼Œçœæ¡æ‰‹ä¹‹è²»ã€‚"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` â€” order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example â€” destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

We need to add support for a json data editor, similar like we have the markdown editor.

* This should be a stand alone component
* when the user clicks on a link that is a json file, the editor should be opened
  * when in card-view, this should be a popup, similar like the card or action popups, so managed by the [card_popup_service.ts](app/src/services/card_popup_service.ts)
  * when in list view, this should be a new tab with a data editor
* for an array, show a table, the columns are the field names of the objects inside the array, if the array has primitives, there is only 1 column, 'values'	
  * user can add & delete, copy, cut, paste records.
  * user can select multiple records for copy, cut or delete
  * fields allow for inline editing
* for objects, show a form, with fields layout out vertically
* if a field value is a list or object, show a button to dig into the value. this is for objects and for lists. 
  * at the top of the data editor is a breadcrumb component that displays the path into the data.
    * user can click on items to go back

## Current state

`MarkdownEditor` renders repository links, but no application route opens project JSON data. List-view tabs support only cards, actions, and agent instruction Markdown. Repository JSON paths may appear in the file-tree folder structure, but arbitrary JSON files are not open documents and cannot be edited there.

`CardPopupService` owns action, card-details, and card-sequence popups. It has no JSON popup entry. Existing storage bridges can list repository paths, load a te
[335 characters omitted]
re` and only render or invoke service operations.
* Intercept clicks on project-local links whose path ends in `.json`, resolving relative paths from the Markdown document containing the link. Keep HTTP, HTTPS, anchor, non-JSON, and paths outside the active project on their current link path.
* In card view, add a `json-data` entry to `CardPopupService` and render the editor in the shared popup stack. In list view, extend `OpenFilesService`, `TabBar`, `TextEditorPane`, and project persistence with a JSON document kind so one tab exists per resolved project-relative path.
* Load JSON through the active storage text-file API. Parse before exposing editable data. Show malformed, missing, and unreadable-file errors through `dialogService`; do not create or mutate editor state during render.
* Save valid JSON through the existing project persistence flow, using stable pretty-printed JSON and a final newline. Read-only projects render data but disable every mutation. If storage reports an external change while the document is dirty, keep the draft and warn instead of overwriting it.
* Render an object as vertically stacked property-name/value rows. Strings, numbers, booleans, and `null` use type-preserving inline controls; property names are not editable in this feature. A root primitive uses the same single-value control.
* Render an array containing only objects as a table whose columns are the union of object field names in first-seen order. Render every other array, including empty and mixed-type arrays, with one `values` column. Missing object fields display an empty cell and remain missing until edited.
* Array selection supports one or many rows. Add inserts an empty object for an object table and `null` for a `values` table. Delete removes selected rows. Copy writes selected values, in row order, as a JSON array. Cut removes rows only after clipboard writing succeeds. Paste accepts a JSON array and inserts its values after the last selected row, or at the end when nothing is selected; invalid clipboard JSON leaves data unchanged and shows an error.
* Replace nested object or array values with a drill-in button. Breadcrumb starts at the file root and adds one item for each property name or array index traversed. Clicking an ancestor item returns to that exact value; edits that remove the current value return the editor to its closest existing ancestor.
* Add focused service and component tests for link routing by workspace view, popup/tab reuse, loading and save failures, object and array layouts, mixed and empty arrays, scalar editing, row operations, clipboard failure, breadcrumbs, read-only behavior, and dirty external changes.

## acceptance criteria

* Clicking a project-local `.json` link in card view opens one managed JSON popup anchored to the clicked link; clicking the same link again activates the existing popup.
* Clicking a project-local `.json` link in list view opens or activates one JSON tab for that resolved path.
* External, anchor, and non-JSON links retain current behavior. Missing, unreadable, or malformed JSON shows a clear error and does not open an editable document.
* Objects display vertical fields. Object-only arrays display a table with the union of their field names. Primitive, mixed, and empty arrays display one `values` column. Root primitive values remain editable.
* Nested objects and arrays open through a drill-in control. Breadcrumb shows each traversed property or index and lets user return to any ancestor.
* User can edit scalar values without changing their JSON type. Array add, multi-row selection, delete, copy, cut, and paste preserve row order and produce valid JSON.
* Invalid edits or clipboard content never change draft data. Failed clipboard writes never remove cut rows.
* Saving writes stable pretty-printed JSON through existing project persistence. Read-only projects cannot change data, and dirty drafts are not overwritten by external file changes.
* JSON popup and tab state survives unrelated React rerenders and closes through existing popup and tab controls.

we just introduced the new json editor. it contains an object editor which shows 2 columns: the fieldname: field value (can be a button.

* first, show the button as links
* add a header
* show in a table style, so horizontal row indicators
* the column resizer jumps back to the original position first when you want to resize, so it is poorly implemented
* the column divider should be a thin line, the drag area may be wider

## Current state

`JsonObjectEditor` renders object properties in a two-column CSS grid without column headers or horizontal row dividers. Nested object and array values use outlined `Open ...` buttons, so navigation controls look heavier than inline values.

The field-name splitter uses the pointer's absolute position inside the editor to calculate column width. Container padding and grid gaps are included in that position but not in the stored width, so the column jumps when dragging starts. The full six-pixel drag target is also painted as the divider, which makes the visible line too heavy.

## implementation details

* Keep object fields in one resizable two-column layout. Add a header row labelled `Field` and `Value`, and separate header and data rows with one-pixel horizontal `divider` lines so the form reads like a table.
* Render nested object and array drill-in controls as link-style text buttons: buttons with hyperlink styling, not URL anchors. Keep their current `document.drillInto` navigation, labels, keyboard access, and focus behavior.
* On pointer down, store both pointer X position and current field-name width. During movement, add pointer delta to stored width, then clamp against existing minimum field and value widths. Pointer up, cancellation, and lost capture end the same bounded drag session.
* Keep a wider splitter hit target for pointer and touch input, but draw a centered one-pixel divider inside it. Use theme `divider` color at rest and `primary.main` for hover, focus, and active states.
* Extend `json_data_editor.test.tsx` with object header, link-style drill-in, no-jump pointer resize, and clamping coverage. Keep existing keyboard resize and breadcrumb navigation behavior. Verify divider thickness, hit-target width, hover, focus, active state, and light and dark themes manually because these are visual styling requirements.

## acceptance criteria

* Object editor shows `Field` and `Value` headers above property rows.
* Each object property row has a horizontal divider, using theme colors in light and dark modes.
* Nested object and array values appear as link-style controls and still open the selected value by pointer or keyboard.
* Starting a drag from any point in splitter hit target keeps current column width until pointer moves; movement changes width only by pointer movement distance.
* Pointer resizing cannot make field-name column narrower than its minimum or leave value column narrower than its minimum. Keyboard resizing keeps same bounds.
* Splitter presents a one-pixel visible divider while retaining wider pointer and touch hit target. Hover, keyboard focus, and active drag remain visible.
* Focused JSON editor tests and `npm run lint` pass.
